NEW RESEARCH: You can now create a new robot optimized for any given task!

I love this new project by @haqhuy, @SongShuran, and others.

Called "Transformer Transformer: A Unified Model for Motion-Conditioned Robot Co-design", it generates a robot's physical design and its controller together from a task spec.

DEFINITIONS:
- Reward function: A scoring rule that assigns a number to how well a behavior achieves the task. Here, it is the objective the generated design is pushed to maximize (e.g., track the target motion with low error).
- Tokenizing: dividing continuous or structured data (a robot's links, joints, motor specs, states, actions) into a discrete vocabulary of symbols a transformer can process, the same step that turned pixels and audio into "language" for these models.
- Diffusion transformer (DiT): A transformer trained to turn random noise into structured output through iterative denoising. Here, it generates robot bodies and trajectories instead of images.
- MuJoCo: The standard fast physics simulator for robotics research (DeepMind-maintained). The Menagerie is its curated zoo of ready-to-use robot models.
- CMA-ES: Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy, the workhorse black-box optimizer: it evolves a population of candidate designs, keeps the best, and needs thousands of simulator rollouts.
- Bimanual multi-trajectory optimization: Finding one design/controller that performs well across several target motions for a two-armed robot at once, harder than optimizing for a single arm and a single motion.
- BERT/MAE masked-modeling trick: Train one model to fill in whatever parts of the input you hide (words for BERT, image patches for MAE); at inference, choosing what to mask chooses the task, so masking the body makes it a designer and masking the actions makes it a controller.

In practice, you give it a target end-effector motion and a reward function, and it outputs a complete embodiment (link, joint, motor, and inertial property), as well as a controller to drive it.

It works by tokenizing both the body (links/joints/motors) and the dynamics (states/actions) into a compact scheme called RoboTokens, training a diffusion transformer (DiT) over them.
The same model predicts dynamics using those predictions ("Dynamics Self-Guidance") to push generated designs toward higher reward at inference time.
Masking different token types (using the BERT/MAE masked-modeling trick) lets the one model do three jobs: generate an embodiment, control an arbitrary embodiment, or design one conditioned on a motion.

It is trained on 11 robots from the MuJoCo Menagerie (0.65 kg hand to 67.5 kg quadruped, 6–35 joints), and validated in sim and on a physical ALOHA doing cloth flinging.

I like the fact that this approach inverts the entire recent robotics ideas: designing a policy for a fixed robot -> designing the robot for a fixed task.
Every other approach assumes the body is given and learns a controller.
Transformer Transformer takes the task (target motion + reward), then generates the body and controller jointly.

In practice, it is a ~180× speedup over the standard optimizer at equal-or-better quality.
It reaches "CMA-ES-level quality in seconds" and finishes bimanual multi-trajectory optimization in <1 min vs CMA-ES's 3+ hours.

Surprisingly, this approach was validated on real hardware!
The generated design was measurably smoother.
On a physical ALOHA flinging cloth (a deformable, dynamic task), the optimized design cut tracking error 73% and peak joint speed 30% versus the original, with fewer joint-speed peaks.
Therefore: real world results, not a sim-only benchmark -> that is worth underlining nowadays!

Also worth mentioning: this is the lab behind UMI and Handroid, that I mentioned here previously!
The team seems extremely creative, i love these out-of-the-box approaches.

5-Picture Cinematic Collage Prompt
Prompt:
Create a single premium five-panel cinematic fashion collage, showing the same beautiful adult South Asian woman in five completely different environments and moods. All five panels must have perfect character consistency — identical facial features, face shape, eyes, nose, lips, hairstyle, skin tone, body proportions, and overall identity. She should look like the exact same woman photographed on the same day.
Panel 1 — Monsoon Romance:
The woman standing outdoors during a gentle monsoon rain, wearing an elegant flowing orange saree with a subtle modern blouse. Wet hair naturally framing her face, tiny raindrops visible in the air, lush green trees behind her, soft cinematic background blur, emotional peaceful expression, natural diffused light.
Panel 2 — Luxury Morning:
The same woman inside a sophisticated modern luxury apartment, wearing an elegant cream-colored dress, sitting beside a large floor-to-ceiling window while enjoying morning coffee. Warm sunlight entering through the glass, minimalist marble interior, contemporary furniture, soft shadows, peaceful sophisticated atmosphere.
Panel 3 — Beach Sunset:
The same woman walking barefoot beside a tropical ocean at golden hour, wearing a flowing white summer dress. Gentle wind moving her hair and dress, warm sunset reflecting across the water, palm trees in the distance, cinematic golden sky, relaxed joyful expression.
Panel 4 — Traditional Evening:
The same woman at an elegant heritage palace courtyard during evening, wearing a luxurious deep-red traditional Indian saree with tasteful jewelry. Warm lanterns, ornate architecture, marble flooring, subtle reflections, dramatic but natural lighting, regal and sophisticated atmosphere.
Panel 5 — Modern City Night:
The same woman standing on a luxurious rooftop overlooking a modern city skyline at night, wearing a sleek black evening gown. City lights creating beautiful bokeh behind her, subtle wind in her hair, sophisticated confident expression, cinematic blue-and-warm ambient lighting, premium fashion editorial atmosphere.
Overall Visual Style
High-end fashion magazine + luxury travel campaign + cinematic photography, photorealistic, natural human skin texture, realistic hair strands, realistic fabric, physically accurate lighting, natural shadows, subtle film grain, atmospheric depth, shallow depth of field, HDR but restrained, professional 35mm and 85mm photography, realistic lens characteristics, premium color grading, extremely detailed, 8K UHD.
Composition:
Five clearly separated but visually connected panels arranged in one elegant 2×3 editorial collage, with the fifth panel occupying the center/bottom position. Seamless premium magazine layout, balanced composition, consistent lighting quality, no panel overpowering the others.
Identity consistency is the highest priority: same woman in every panel, no changes to facial structure, age, hairstyle, skin tone, eye shape, body proportions, or identity.
Negative prompt:
cartoon, anime, CGI, plastic skin, artificial face, different woman, inconsistent identity, changing facial features, different hairstyle, distorted face, asymmetrical eyes, bad anatomy, extra fingers, missing fingers, deformed hands, duplicated limbs, unnatural body, blurry face, low resolution, oversaturated colors, excessive HDR, harsh artificial lighting, unrealistic reflections, text, captions, typography, watermark, logo, signature.

I built MirrorProof; a trust layer for AI clothing virtual try on.

Virtual try on can generate an nice image, but it rarely answers the important question:
Did the virtual preview accurately represent what the customer actually received?

Most virtual try on products stop after generating the preview.
MirrorProof introduces a second stage: after the garment arrives, the shopper uploads a new photo while physically wearing it.
The application then compares the preview with reality.

The workflow is simple:
* Upload a consented person photo
* Upload the garment image
* Generate a live YouCam preview
*Save the verification
* Upload a physical wearing photo
* Review the visible differences

The virtual preview comes from the live YouCam API, while the reliability result is calculated from the images submitted during that verification.
If no real comparison exists, no score is shown.

The Preview Reliability Score combines five visible consistency metrics:
* Colour - 30%
* Pattern and texture - 25%
* Silhouette -20%
* Garment length - 15%
* Person preservation - 10%

The weights are versioned and explainable.

MirrorProof also calculates analysis confidence, before presenting a score, it checks factors such as:
* Resolution
* Lighting
* Sharpness
* Torso visibility
* Image alignment
* Obstructions
* Whether the two images are actually different

The result is designed to be inspectable not just impressive.

The users receive:

* An overall reliability score
* Analysis confidence
* Five component scores
* Plain-language explanations
* A preview-versus-reality slider
* Clear limitations

MirrorProof is deliberately honest about what it cannot measure.
It does not guarantee:
*  Exact sizing
* Comfort
* Fabric quality
* Construction quality
* Stretch
* Medical suitability
* How the garment behaves during movement

Privacy is also important.
The physical comparison is processed transiently in server memory and is not uploaded to Supabase by that step.
YouCam separately processes the source images required to generate the virtual preview, and API credentials remain server-side.

There is also a retailer evidence view.
Retailers can review completed comparisons, average reliability, confidence, weak metrics and product-level status.

AI IS CHANGING FASHION, AND IT’S BIGGER THAN IMAGE GENERATION.🧵

Artificial Intelligence is quietly transforming almost every stage of the fashion value chain.

From design and trend forecasting to marketing, production, e-commerce, and customer experience, AI is changing how fashion businesses operate.

🧵Here are a few areas where the impact is already visible:

🔹 Design & Ideation:- Exploring silhouettes, patterns, colors, and collection concepts faster.

🔹 Trend Forecasting:-  Using data to identify emerging consumer preferences and market trends.

🔹 Virtual Prototyping:-  Visualizing designs before spending heavily on materials and production.

🔹 Personalization:- Helping brands recommend products and experiences based on customer preferences.

🔹 Marketing & Content:-  Accelerating campaign concepts, storytelling, product descriptions, and visual development.

🔹 Demand Forecasting:- Helping brands make smarter production and inventory decisions, potentially reducing waste.

But here’s what I find most interesting:

AI may not replace the fashion designer. It may replace some of the limitations that slow the designer down.

Creativity still requires taste.

Culture still requires understanding.

Craftsmanship still requires skill.

And strategy still requires human judgment.

For African fashion, this presents an even bigger opportunity.

Imagine combining African heritage, traditional craftsmanship, modern design thinking, and AI-powered innovation to build globally competitive fashion brands.

The question is no longer:

“Will AI affect fashion?”

It already is.

The better question is:

👉🏼How will fashion entrepreneurs use AI to build better brands, products, and businesses?”

Pick the picture you want to use and upload it to Grok, ChatGPT, or any AI tool you want to use. 

Then explain exactly what you have in mind,  the outfit, location, pose, hairstyle, lighting, background, mood, and every other detail.

Just describe what you want in your own words and ask the AI to turn your explanation into a detailed image-generation prompt.

A simple formula is:

Subject + outfit + pose + location + lighting + camera style + mood + details.

For example:

“Use my uploaded photo as the face reference. Create a realistic full-body portrait of me wearing a classy black gown, standing in a luxurious hotel lobby. Soft warm lighting, elegant pose, natural skin texture, realistic proportions, high-end fashion photography, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, ultra-realistic.”

If you want the AI to maintain your appearance, you can add:

“Keep my facial features and identity consistent with the reference photo.”

That’s basically it. Describe the picture in your head, let the AI structure the prompt, then use the prompt to generate your image.

Native ads are one of the hardest ones to make actually work.

The image part is easy, just create a batch of 20 variants. Done. But the hard part is the storytelling and taking a reader from unaware to fully aware.

My ideal set up for the copy is:

1. Hook -> STOP the scroll + create curiosity
2. Problem -> Make them recognize themselves
3. Failed solutions -> WHY what they tried didn't work
4. Mechanism -> Explain what's ACTUALLY causing the problem
5. Solution -> Introduce your product naturally
6. Proof -> Reviews / authority / results
7. Offer -> Give them a reason to take action

The magic happens in the storytelling. Make it personal so someone from your ICP can literally think: “this is me.”

Talking in the same language as your ICP makes the storytelling actually stick (so research the keywords/language your audience uses in FB groups, Reddit etc). 

We often see that a PDP works best in these cases when the copy is good. Bc the long-form primary text basically works as your prelander.
